what: Plan section 7.31: blind 50-agreement M13 holdout under schema v2.15, the 7.30 stage 1 (prepare_v7 with mae_sections and mae_definition_leaves, unioned with the Haiku picker) and every post-check in postchecks.py including v2.1 rule 11; Sonnet extraction from candidates, Opus gold from full text, Opus adjudication; pooled with M7 to M12 (342 US agreements).
run_notes: Run split across two accounts: the first stopped at its weekly limit with 11 extractions missing (batches hit 429s); those 11 were re-extracted in four new batches with the same brief.
A dead extractor's half-written helper (_b3q7_gen.py, for b8faf5bc) was found in out/sonnet and deleted unused; b8faf5bc was re-extracted from scratch.
Every extraction and gold file was validated: ten concepts, agreement id, every quote and quote_end verbatim on one line of its input.
Extraction batch 4 read part of another Sonnet extraction (5ed13dbd); a rerun batch viewed the first five lines of another Sonnet file (00247e5c). Neither read gold, so the run stays blind.
Token logging is incomplete: gold batch 13 and most first-account extraction batches were not logged.

postcheck_verdicts.0a91852c v2.2 rule 12: wrong (termination rights never use the defined Adverse Recommendation Change)
postcheck_verdicts.de5d8138 v2.5 rule 3: wrong (sufficiency rep counts the target's cash)

verdicts.correct_value: approval_failure_with_tail, breach_of_no_shop, buyer_breach, buyer_recommendation_change, outside_date_with_tail, recommendation_failure
verdicts.reason: The trigger is a change in the Parent (buyer-side) recommendation on a reverse fee, which the schema codes buyer_recommendation_change, not the target-fee code adverse_recommendation_change.

The extension applies when 'the conditions set forth in Sections 8.01(e) and (f) or Section 8.03(d)' are unsatisfied: one test led by the HSR/no-order conditions with the related Debt Exchange separation condition, which v2.13 rule 6 codes regulatory_pending. It is not alternative extension routes under rule 1.

verdicts.correct_value: clause (a) of both definitions is industry, change_in_law and other
verdicts.reason: Clause (a) also carves out 'changes in the price of commodities or raw materials', which fits no listed code and is other; the text is in the candidates.

verdicts.correct_value: add the Option Holder cap entry: the Option Holder's deemed contribution to the Escrow Account, amount not_stated, basis formula
verdicts.reason: Section 11.5(e) separately caps each Option Holder at its deemed contribution to the Escrow Account; each indemnitor's cap is its own entry. The extractor mentioned it only in notes.

verdicts.correct_value: as gold: Snacks Business MAE carve-outs (a)-(j) coded, prospects false, ability_to_consummate false, disproportionate exception for (a), (b), (c), (d) and (j)
verdicts.reason: Both MAE definitions are in S120 of the full text, which is not in the candidates, so the extractor coded every field not_stated; gold codes them from the definition.

Section 9.11 makes Parent jointly and severally liable for Purchaser's obligations and Section 1.1(f) has Parent provide Purchaser the funds; a parent guarantee or affiliate funding covenant is other (v2.8 rule 1, v2.9 rule 9).

verdicts.correct_value: CBA MAE includes industry (no stock price); Pubco MAE includes stock_price_or_volume (no industry), in both arms
verdicts.reason: Per defined term, both arms code identical carve-out categories; the diff comes from party_side (gold puts both terms target_side in this double-dummy deal, the extractor puts CBA buyer_side), which shifted how the definitions were matched.

Section 8.1(a)(iv) covers the Purchaser's failure to close 'whether as a result of a Financing Failure or otherwise', so one right covers both events and gets one code per matching event (failure_to_close and financing_failure). The extractor folded the financing failure into failure_to_close.

The only breach bars are the mirrored 'was caused by the failure ... to fulfill any material obligation ... or by ... material breach' provisos (cause_or_result). Clause (y), which bars the Purchaser when all 7.2 conditions are satisfied and the Sellers are ready to close, is not a breach test, and gold's own note said so; gold fixed.

verdicts.correct_value: 2 definitions; target MAE carve-outs (b)-(i) [announcement_or_pendency, buyer_action_or_request, change_in_gaap, change_in_law, compliance_with_agreement, financial_markets, industry, natural_disaster, other, political_war_terrorism] with a disproportionate-effect proviso on (a)-(e) and (g); buyer_side lowercase entry
verdicts.reason: S121 (in candidates, groups=resolved) holds the rest of the MAE definition from clause (b) on, with the carve-outs and the disproportionate-effect proviso; the extractor treated the definition as missing. The Purchaser has no defined MAE term, and its non-contravention rep 2.2(b) uses 'material adverse effect on the Purchaser's ability to perform' operatively, so v2.15 rule 1 adds a buyer_side entry.

The definition's opening (the prongs) falls on a page missing from the text, so the target entry's prongs are unknown; gold's per-prong not_stated and the extractor's whole-prongs not_stated (read as null) say the same thing.

verdicts.correct_value: 2 (Company Material Adverse Effect target_side; Parent Material Adverse Effect buyer_side)
verdicts.reason: Section 9.03 defines only a generic 'Material Adverse Effect' on a person, but the agreement uses 'Company Material Adverse Effect' and 'Parent Material Adverse Effect' operatively, each '(as defined in Section 9.03)', and the generic term appears alone only in a covenant. That is the v2.15 rule 2 case of party terms built on one generic definition (as in the M11 Glass/Solstice ruling), so one entry per party term.

Clause (iii) 'national or international political or social conditions' is political_war_terrorism alone (v2.11 rule 4); gold has coded the same wording that way in M11 and M12, never adding other for 'social'. Gold fixed in both synonym entries and in the disproportionate-effect applies_to.

verdicts.correct_value: {value: false, quote: 'their respective obligations to consummate the Transactions are not subject to any condition or contingency with respect to receipt of the Debt Financing or any financing or funding by any third party'}
verdicts.reason: Section 6.15(e) says expressly that Parent's and Merger Sub's obligations are not subject to any financing condition, so financing_condition is false with that quote (v2.1 rule 2). Gold's note missed the sentence; gold fixed, and no_financing_condition_statement set to true from the same quote.

The definition sits inside Section 4.1 (S10, in candidates): prong (ii) is 'the ability of such Party to timely consummate', there is no prospects prong, and the one proviso carves out execution, announcement or consummation. The extractor did not find the definition and left everything not_stated.

The definitions section states "Company Termination Compensation" means an amount in cash equal to $72,600,000; that definition is in the text but not in the candidates file, so the extractor wrongly called it not_stated.

The definitions section states "Parent Termination Compensation" means an amount in cash equal to $254,300,000; the definition was not retrieved into the candidates, so the extractor recorded not_stated.

verdicts.correct_value: first extension condition: other (gold) or regulatory_pending (extractor)
verdicts.reason: The 90-day extension applies when only the Offer Condition in paragraph (B) of ANNEX I is unmet, and Annex I is not in the text; indirect cues (grouping with the Legal Restraints condition (C) as slow-to-satisfy conditions) suggest a regulatory condition, but v2.13 rule 3 assumes the cited condition can be read, and the schema does not say whether to infer its kind or treat it as defined outside the text.

The "Deposit" definition says the Deposit "shall be increased to $25,000,000" if the Termination Date is extended, so the amount the Sellers retain is $25,000,000 in that case; the $15,000,000 is only the further installment. The definition line is not in the candidates file.

The undefined lowercase material adverse change is also used operatively in the absence-of-changes representation 2.1(g) ("business, assets or prospects of Sellers"), and v2.11 rule 2 codes it from the words where it is used; that representation (S8) is not in the candidates file.

verdicts.correct_value: gold's coding of the S15 definition: six carve-outs, prospects false, ability_to_consummate true, disproportionate exception for (A)-(C)
verdicts.reason: "Material Adverse Effect" is defined in Section 3.1(a) (S15), which is in the candidates file, with a business prong (no prospects), an ability-to-consummate prong, carve-outs (A) to (F) and a disproportionate-effect proviso for (A) to (C); the extractor wrongly said it was undefined.

12.5 lets Seller, at its option, seek specific performance, declare the Deposit forfeited, or pursue other remedies; these are listed as alternatives, and the text never says forfeiture is in addition to other remedies or cumulative, so the remedy rule gives not_stated rather than non_exclusive.

verdicts.correct_value: {"amount": 250000, "currency": "USD", "basis": "fixed", "pct": null} per Alleged Environmental Defect (7.2), counts_toward_basket not_stated; $200,000 per title defect in notes
verdicts.reason: 7.2 (S33) defines an Alleged Environmental Defect only where each individual defect reaches $250,000, a per-item threshold on the defects that feed the $50,000,000 deductible, so gold's de minimis is sound. S33 is not in the candidates file, and the extractor's note says the per-defect minimums sat outside the candidates.

verdicts.correct_value: adverse_recommendation_change, approval_failure_with_tail, breach_no_tail, breach_of_no_shop, breach_with_tail, outside_date_with_tail, recommendation_failure, superior_proposal_termination
verdicts.reason: 9.3(c)(ii) makes half the fee payable within two business days of a Parent termination under 9.1(f) for breach of representations or covenants, with no later deal required, which is breach_no_tail (v2.2 rule 11); the tail on the remaining half is the separate breach_with_tail. The extractor described the no-tail half in its notes but did not code it.

Besides the 5.9 funds representation (cash_on_hand), 2.5(a) has Parent covenant to provide Purchaser (the merger sub) the funds required for the Paying Agent, an affiliate covenant to fund that v2.9 rule 9 codes other. The extractor reviewed S13 but did not add it.

This is an all-stock reverse merger in which Parent pays no cash (no cash even for fractional shares), so there is no acquisition financing. The Concurrent PIPE, its $50,000,000 minimum-proceeds condition and the mutual Permitted Financing cooperation covenant fund the combined company, and v2.2 rule 9 says a minimum-offering condition in a stock-for-stock deal with no buyer cash obligation does not make financing present.

The 5.8(i) sufficiency representation counts the Financing 'together with available cash of the Company', which is the target's cash, not the buyer's, so v2.12 rule 1 adds no cash_on_hand. The extractor's own note reached the same conclusion; the cash_on_hand entry was added by a post-check (tagged v2.5 rule 3) that fired wrongly.

verdicts.correct_value: one extension: automatic, condition other (specific performance pending)
verdicts.reason: Section 13.20(b) automatically extends the Outside Date while a specific-performance action is pending; v2.5 rule 8 and v2.13 rule 2 make it an extension entry wherever it sits. Gold fixed.
Clause (viii) names 'national calamity' and v2.3 rule 11 codes 'calamity' as natural_disaster; the extractor coded only political_war_terrorism.

verdicts.correct_value: adds other for Company Triggering Event (v), entering a letter of intent or Contract for a Company Acquisition Proposal
verdicts.reason: The 7.1(d) fee trigger reaches every Company Triggering Event, and clause (v) (entering an LOI or contract for a competing proposal) fits no listed code, so it is other; the definition is in candidate section S87, which the extractor quoted.

verdicts.correct_value: definition in Exhibit A S87: ability-to-consummate prong true, no prospects, carve-outs announcement_or_pendency, stock_price_or_volume, industry, general_economic, financial_markets, disproportionate proviso on (C) and (D)
verdicts.reason: The MAE definition is in S87 of the full text but the candidate file carries only S87's heading line, so the extractor coded it as defined outside the text.

One defined term, 'Material Adverse Effect', is defined in two separate sentences, one 'on the Acquired Corporations' and one 'on Parent', with different prongs; v2.15 rule 2 counts defined terms and gives 'both' for one term applied alike, but does not address one term defined differently per party. Gold left at two entries.

The fee triggers 6.1(g) and 6.1(h) speak only of withdrawing or modifying the recommendation or approving a superior transaction and never use the defined 'Adverse Recommendation Change' (4.5(c), which includes failing to recommend against a competing transaction), so v2.2 rule 12 does not apply; the post-check added recommendation_failure wrongly.

verdicts.correct_value: carve-out (H) is announcement_or_pendency plus compliance_with_agreement; no other
verdicts.reason: Clause (H)'s 'including reasonable expenses incurred by the Parties hereto in consummating the transactions' illustrates the effects of the announcement and consummation already coded (v2.3 rule 11) and adds no separate category. Gold fixed.

Section 9.4(b)(iii) makes general-rep claims go 'first' to the Indemnity Escrow Fund and then makes the Securityholders 'directly liable for the remaining excess', and Section 9.3(a) calls the escrow only 'partial security', so the value is false under v2.5 rule 6, v2.8 rule 8 and v2.9 rule 5 even though the 9.6(a) cap equals the escrow amount. The extractor quoted the order and overrode it.

The whole election clause (Section 7.10, S80) is in the text and assigns no tax cost of the 338(g) election to either party, so tax_cost_shift is none under v2.2 rule 5, as in the earlier ruling on 5338e50e.

Clause (i) also carves out 'any shutdown or material limiting of U.S. or foreign federal, state or local government services', which no listed category fits, so it adds 'other' under the common rule on coded fields. The extractor's text for clause (i) leaves the shutdown out.

The recitals say LKCM Headwater Investments IV, L.P. is 'guaranteeing, among other things, Parent's obligation to pay the Reverse Termination Fee', and v2.8 rule 1 codes an affiliate's guarantee of the buyer's payment obligations as committed financing 'other', which matches how gold coded limited guarantees in M11 and M12. The extractor saw the Limited Guarantee and dismissed it.

Section 9.01(b)(i) has two separately lettered extensions with their own tests and lengths: (x) one month if the Marketing Period has begun but not ended, and (y) no Outside Date sooner than three Business Days after the Marketing Period ends. Under v2.13 rule 1, extensions drafted separately are separate entries. The extractor folded (y) into notes.

The Limited Guarantees from the Veritas and Elliott funds guarantee 'certain of Parent's and Sub's payment obligations under this Agreement', which v2.8 rule 1 codes as committed financing 'other', consistent with M11 and M12 gold. The extractor saw the guarantees and dismissed them.
